verdict.rationale: Jan's first-party docs describe a built-in, OpenAI-compatible API server that runs locally at localhost:1337, powered by llama.cpp. It documents /v1/models and /v1/chat/completions endpoints (with streaming and tool calling), a configurable /v1 prefix, and an option to expose the server on the local network. This clearly delivers the core story of launching a local OpenAI-compatible server for local models. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that any loaded model is automatically exposed through the server, step-by-step launch instructions in the evidence, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can launch a local OpenAI-compatible API server for any loaded model

citations.quote: Jan provides a built-in, OpenAI-compatible API server that runs entirely on your computer, powered by `llama.cpp`. Use it as a drop-in replacement for cloud APIs
OpenAI-Compatible API: Local server at `localhost:1337` for other applications
Jan's local API server exposes an OpenAI-compatible REST API at http://127.0.0.1:1337.
/v1 (Default): Follows OpenAI's convention. The chat completions endpoint would be http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1/chat/completions.
